A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Scaling Laws for Optimal Data Mixtures. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and some relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM, native multimodal, and vision-model training results, scaling-law prediction errors, optimized-mixture evaluations, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds Regmix comparison results in Appendix B.1, Table 13.

M1.justification: The additive and joint scaling laws, Huber-loss fitting with basin-hopping and L-BFGS, and mirror-descent mixture optimization are unchanged. The new Regmix comparator and codebase disclosure do not alter the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Training domains and evaluation tasks remain unchanged across language, multimodal, and vision experiments. The additional downstream benchmarks displayed in v2 Table 3 were already reported in v1 Appendix C, Table 15.

E2.justification: Appendix B.1 and Table 13 add Regmix (Liu et al., 2024), described as a linear loss predictor, alongside the existing Ye M1–M4 comparisons. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The Regmix comparison uses the existing 200M-parameter, 8B-token setting with 25 fitting mixtures and 59 test mixtures. Training hyperparameters and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. V2 Table 1 newly tabulates a 7B/150B configuration already described in v1 Section 5.

E4.justification: Section 4 adds a computational-cost analysis comparing the small-model experiments used to fit the laws with larger-model runs, supported by Table 1's FLOP totals. Existing mixture-count sensitivity, cosine-schedule validation, alternative-law analyses, and optimal-mixture investigations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains 100 random trials, median curves, and 25–75% quantile bands. No changes to repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical reporting practices are documented.

E6.justification: Table 13 adds Regmix test MREs of 1.31%, 1.35%, 0.92%, and 0.89% for Wikipedia, GitHub, StackExchange, and PG-19, respectively; the retained additive results are 0.18%, 0.19%, 0.18%, and 0.12%. Table 1 also adds FLOP totals. Existing numerical performance results, including the relocated downstream benchmark table, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, asymptotic cross-entropy decomposition, and weighted-target optimization are retained. V1 equations (12) and (13) become v2 equations (6.4) and (C.1), without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: predicting loss from model size, token budget, and mixture weights; extrapolating across mixtures and scales; and selecting optimal mixtures across three model modalities.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly states that the cosine schedule prevents scaling-law extrapolation for the 7B experiment. Section 6 replaces v1's accuracy-versus-simplicity rationale with a claim that the full law extrapolates worse than the joint law, although unchanged Table 4 gives lower LLM MRE for the full law: 1.21% versus 1.30%. The main limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly identifies L3M as the training codebase and supplies a repository reference. Section 4 and Table 1 add computational-budget accounting. These improve documentation; the existing hyperparameter tables do not establish changes to training.

R1.justification: V2 adds the L3M reference and explicitly discusses the already-cited Regmix work in Appendix B.1 as an evaluated comparator. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized rewrites, author-year citations, front-matter and acknowledgement edits, and appendix consolidation after moving the downstream-results table into the main text.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an Apple-branded front page and changes typography, margins, caption styling, figure sizes, and float placement throughout. V1 Table 15 replaces the shorter main-text Table 3; Table 1 gains a FLOPs column; Table 13 gains Regmix rows. Existing figures are redistributed, with Figures 5 and 6 exchanging numbers.

improvement.justification: The added Regmix comparison, quantitative cost accounting, and L3M reference modestly improve empirical assessment and reproducibility. These gains are partly offset by the revised Section 6 interpretation, which conflicts with the unchanged full-versus-joint LLM results in Table 4. Overall, the added evidence and transparency provide a limited improvement; the central method and existing results remain stable.
